result:
Round 352 is planned, and the decision is **CONTINUE**. It fixes the bug C confirmed in round 351 (C-R351-01, Medium); RETRO moves to round 353.

**What happened in round 351:** the round failed. A stopped because its code-reviewer found that test DP72 checks nothing between releasing the drag and pressing Undo. So a release that seeks the video back to the old position, or an Undo that writes nothing, would go unnoticed. C confirmed this by reading the test. The fault is mine, not A's: lesson 58 says I review my sketch before dispatch, and in round 350 I didn't. C did not run the mutant and names browser checks, so `browserVerified` is false. Gate 351 was skipped, so the baseline is still `7f56989` plus the 3 changed files, and the dock file is unchanged. Nothing moved to done in the backlog.

**Round 352 (test and doc only; the dock and `ArrangementContext.tsx` stay byte-identical):**
- **The test change:** A applies two patches unchanged:
  - `b-round-351/sketch-dp72-release.patch.txt` (17 lines added, 9 removed);
  - `b-round-351/sketch-doc232.patch.txt`.

  The new DP72 checks four things:
  - only real `<video>` writes are counted;
  - releasing the drag writes no new seek (checked after a 20 ms wait), and the clip lands where the preview showed it;
  - Undo writes a new seek;
  - that seek is back at the pre-drag time.

  The patch also takes the reviewer's two Low notes (the global spy and the try/finally).
- **My checks on a scratch copy:** the whole file passes 74/74, with no tsc errors, Biome clean, and DP72 green 3 times in a row.
- **Proof the gap is closed:** with the reader's base swapped to `arrangement` (mutant M-B1), round 351's DP72 still passed, and the new one fails at the release check.
- **Other mutants:** M-B6 (release commits the old arrangement) fails the clip-position check, and M-B7 (Undo writes nothing) fails DP72 alone. The four existing mutants give the same red sets as before.
- **Sketch review:** this time I had the sketch reviewed before dispatch. I used `tech-lead`, because `code-reviewer` isn't on my consult list. It found nothing Medium or higher. I applied its Low 1 (count the writes after release, not just the last value), which is what makes M-B1 fail. Its other Low is ruled in the task, so A's reviewer can't stop the round on either one again. It reviewed the first form of the sketch; the only change since is its own Low 1, and the task says so.
- **Doc 232 status line:** A asked whether the task text or lesson 28 wins. I kept the doc's published form, now `C round 352 pending`. The conflict with lesson 28 goes to RETRO 353 to settle.
- **C's rows:** the claims script `b-round-351/claims-352.sh`, source scope, the whole file 74/74, and control plus 7 mutants. The browser rows skipped in round 351 come back: the M-B2′ names probe on a scratch server, the names smoke at 1440, and the anonymous-auth check at both window sizes.

**Files I wrote:**
- the old task archived as `tasks/round-351.md` (byte-equal copy);
- the new `current-task.md`;
- `b-round-351.md`, `b-next.json`;
- everything in `b-round-351/`: claims script and expected outputs, both patches, the mutant diffs and logs, the sketch review, and the two update scripts;
- `backlog.json` (v314, decisions D-29z1123…D-29z1126) and `feature-status.md`.

The store tree still has exactly the same 3 changed files; I edited no app code.

**Also:**
- The advisor was available and I used it twice: once before writing and once to review. It caught a wrong line count (I had written 16/8; it is 17/9), which I corrected in all three places.
- RETRO has now slipped twice and its window is rounds 336–352; the overdue question to Saba (ROOT-REQ-PERF-TIMEOUT) moves with it.
- The next regression round is due on or after 2026-11-08.
- Nothing is ready for root to commit until C passes round 352.
